transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-07
Start: 09:23 PST
Duration: ~65 minutes
Attendees: Sam (Redwood AE), Lena (Redwood SE), Noah (Product), Emily (Eng Lead), Priya (Nexa CTO), Markus (Nexa Platform), Diana (Nexa Product), Omar (Nexa SRE)

Summary:
Quick internal product/eng sync to finalize Q1 roadmap items, review launch readiness checklist for the pilot with Nexa Labs, and follow up on the recent incident that surfaced KV-cache edge cases. Action items captured at end. Transcript below is auto-generated and contains minor transcription errors.

[00:00] Sam: okay everyone, thanks for joining, we wanna focus on the Q1 rollout plan and the readiness items for the Nexa pilot, and go through the incident postmortem stuff quick. we have about an hour.
[00:18] Priya: thanks Sam, excited to sync - high level from Nexa side we want predictable latencies under 200ms p95 for the customer facing query path and cost per 1k calls to be within our target - that is the reason we're considering Redwood dedicated or private.
[00:32] Lena: yup, important to call out that our dedicated pool and private options have slightly different perf and cost profiles - we can do a canary on hosted first but for data residency we might need VPC/private.
[00:45] Markus: quick note, our infra has a limit on concurrent GPU nodes during Q1, so autoscale bursts are risky unless we reserve capacity; would like to see resource numbers.
[00:58] Sam: understood. Noah, you were going to run through the roadmap items?
[01:05] Noah: yeah I'll go quick. Top priorities for Q1: 1) pilot with Nexa - ga criteria and success metrics, 2) launch readiness - runbooks, monitoring and SLOs, 3) performance work - KV cache tuning and batching, 4) enterprise features backlog (SAML, audit logs). We want to sync on owners and dates.
[01:28] Diana: for success metrics we basically need uptime 99.9% during pilot, p95 latency <200ms for short-context queries (<=512 tokens), and model output quality pass rate on our evals > 92%.
[01:45] Emily: on the incident follow-up - last week we saw a KV cache invalidation that caused tail latency spikes when sequence lengths increased unexpectedly. we have a tentative fix but need to verify in staging.
[02:02] Omar: yeah, I filed the incident, root cause points at our cache eviction policy plus a bug in how we handle partial KV rehydration on node failover. attaching the postmortem link in the notes after.
[02:18] Lena: rough numbers: on Redwood Dedicated when batching is tuned for our typical distribution, we see about 25-30% cost reduction vs naive per-request runs. but that depends on sequence concurrency and the KV hit-rate. i need to pull the 512-token and 1024-token bench numbers for you, i have approximate ones locally.
[02:42] Priya: ok that cost delta helps. i also want to understand encrypted-at-rest model and request logs and KMS -- are we able to integrate with our HSM?
[02:52] Sam: yes, Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS/HSM integrations; we have an enterprise security pack and audit-logs. i'll share the security brief.
[03:03] Priya: perfect. Markus, what's the constraint on the infra?
[03:10] Markus: we can commit to a small reserved pool for pilot but not a full dedicated fleet; short term we need predictable throughput for the 8am-6pm PST window. any autoscale beyond that will require ok from infra finance.
[03:25] Noah: so action is figure out the minimum reserved instance size for Redwood Dedicated to meet p95 <200ms given our expected QPS. Lena can run benchmarks with our traffic shape.
[03:36] Lena: yeah i'll do that. the plan: run microbenchmarks with fixed concurrency shapes, test prefix caching scenarios, test KV cache hit/miss distributions, then run end-to-end inside a VPC snapshot with Nexa's infra. i'll need the VPC network diagram and firewall rules from Markus.
[03:55] Markus: i'll send the diagram and firewall rules.
[04:01] Sam: quick note on rollout strategy: canary -> controlled ramp -> GA. canary will be hosted variant with sampling, controlled ramp is dedicated pool or private depending on infra signoff. We'll keep model versions pinned and have auto-fallback to a cheaper variant if perf regresses.
[04:19] Diana: question on regression detection - how fast can we get alerts on quality regressions?
[04:25] Lena: we have eval hooks tied to prompt sets; we can do nightly checks and immediate alerts if key metrics degrade beyond thresholds. depending on traffic we can also stream sample prompts to the eval harness.
[04:39] Priya: ok good. about the incident, do we need runbook changes?
[04:44] Omar: yes, add steps for partial KV rehydration, node failover handling, and a pre-mortem check for large sequence URL variants. i'll update the runbook.
[04:55] Emily: and i want to add that we should include a post-deploy smoke that exercises cold cache paths to catch this earlier.
[05:04] Sam: good, include that in launch checklist.
[05:08] -- long section of technical points and occasional cross-talk, some transcriptions imperfect --
[05:08] [05:08] Lena: (over) the kernel selection for attention ops also has an impact - on A100 we favor the fused kernels, on older cards the fallback path increases token latency by 10-15%. we'll include hardware profile in the benchmark.
[05:30] Markus: re: VPC, we also need to confirm egress IPs for allowlists; if private deploys live in our account we still need clear network boundaries.
[05:40] Sam: noted. on metrics and dashboards, Redwood Console exposes per-route token latency breakdowns and cost; we can give Nexa a template dashboard.
[05:51] Priya: we'd like logs forwarded to our Splunk instance and S3 for audits.
[05:56] Sam: supported; we'll prepare the integration notes.
[06:02] Diana: timeline question - when can we start the pilot?
[06:06] Sam: if we get infra diagrams and signoff this week, Lena can run bench next week, then canary the following week. realistic pilot start: week of 2026-12-21.
[06:18] Priya: that timeline works, assuming the regulatory check isn't a blocker.
[06:22] Noah: i'll coordinate the stakeholder signoff and the launch readiness checklist - will circulate by Friday.
[06:30] Sam: ok let's recap next steps and owners.
[06:33] [06:33] RECAP / NEXT STEPS:
- Sam: share Q1 roadmap deck and security brief (KMS/HSM + audit logs) - due 2026-12-09
- Lena: run KV cache + batching benchmarks (512/1024 tokens) and run VPC-style end-to-end perf tests with Nexa infra - results by 2026-12-14
- Markus: send VPC diagram, firewall rules, infra constraints doc - due 2026-12-09
- Noah: compile and distribute launch readiness checklist and GA success metrics - due 2026-12-11
- Diana/Priya: confirm success metrics and regulatory scoping for pilot - due 2026-12-10
- Omar: update runbook + postmortem items and schedule a follow-up incident review - due 2026-12-10

[06:55] Meeting end: thanks everyone. shared links: (auto) Postmortem doc: https://redwood.internal/pm/INC-2026-11-30, Q1 roadmap draft (internal): https://redwood.internal/docs/q1-roadmap, security brief: https://redwood.internal/security/enterprise-pack.

Note: transcription has some mis-heard acronyms (VPC sometimes as V-PC, KV cache as K-V cache), and a few speaker attribution errors in middle portion.
